text: 192.168.0.114 sends four ICMP echo requests, one second apart, to its gateway 192.168.0.1.
source_text: It sent four ICMP echo requests one second apart and the gateway answered each with an echo reply in about 1 to 2 milliseconds.

text: 192.168.0.1 answers each echo request with an ICMP echo reply to 192.168.0.114 within 1 to 2 milliseconds.
source_text: It sent four ICMP echo requests one second apart and the gateway answered each with an echo reply in about 1 to 2 milliseconds.

text: 192.168.0.114 sends four ICMP echo requests, one second apart, to the external host 72.14.207.99.
source_text: About three seconds later the workstation pinged the external address 72.14.207.99, a Google server, again four echo requests one second apart.

text: 72.14.207.99 answers each echo request with an ICMP echo reply after 62 to 81 milliseconds, arriving with TTL 232.
source_text: Each was answered in 62 to 81 milliseconds. The replies arrived with a TTL of 232, consistent with a remote host many hops away, while the gateway's replies had a TTL of 127.

text: All eight echo requests use the same ICMP identifier with sequence numbers 1 to 8, and every frame is 74 bytes with 32 bytes of data.
source_text: All eight requests share one ICMP identifier and consecutive sequence numbers 1 to 8, as produced by the Windows ping utility, and every frame is 74 bytes long (32 bytes of padding data).
